title: Backfill Sentinel — Weekly check-in and ops notes (2026-02-11)
content:
Attendees: Ava, Daniel, Priya, Marcus, Zoe

Purpose: quick weekly check-in for the Backfill Sentinel initiative — capture anomalous signals from regional backfills, surface work-in-progress heuristics and small experiments that should be elevated to the capacity forum. This is a working notes doc (scratch), will push cleaned summary to the infra weekly digest if any items need escalation.

1) Short summary (tl;dr)
- Observed a 12% increase in partial-backfill events in eu-west-1 over the last 72h (spike centered around 2026-02-09 03:00–05:00 UTC).
- Latency tail for 8k token chat jobs rose ~18% for requests routed to warm-backed nodes that underwent backfill within last 30s.
- Preliminary root cause looks like a combo of: aggressive spot preemption from provider + our slot-consolidation adjustment (rollout 2026-02-05).
- Actionable: rollback slot-consolidation knob to previous threshold for eu-west-1; enable ephemeral warm-pool markers to avoid routing primed requests to nodes in active backfill window.

2) Observations and signal notes
- Signal details: backfill-count (per region) and partial-backfill-ratio both peaked; partial-backfill-ratio defined as fraction of backfills where KV cache was invalidated for >50% of resident sessions.
- Correlated event: provider preemptible-burst (GCP spot-like) showed increased evictions at same window; cross-check with provider events pending.
- Client visible impact: a small subset of customers on dedicated pools (mixed-commit) saw increased retries and a handful of error-rate alerts (5 total pages between 03:10–04:40 UTC).
- Metric artifacts: heatmap and timestamped trace links stored in /ops/observability/backfill-sentinel/2026-02-09; will pin to ticket JIRA-OPS-2147.

3) Recent experiments (notes)
- slot-consolidation-adjustment (rolled 2026-02-05): reduces number of hot slots by 18% to improve utilization. Hypothesis: tighter consolidation reduces idle tokens but increases eviction blast radius when a preemption occurs.
- ephemeral-warmpool-ttl (A/B): added short-lived warm markers to track which nodes had recent KV priming. Early data: requests routed to nodes with warm marker within 60s have 25% lower tail latency. But markers are being lost on backfill.
- eviction-favoring-policy (mini-run): attempted to prefer preemption of non-primed nodes; telemetry shows provider preemptions are not controllable enough to satisfy policy.

4) Immediate action items (owner / ETA)
- Rollback slot-consolidation knob in eu-west-1 to previous values (Daniel Kim) — ETA 2026-02-12 10:00 UTC. Monitor 24h after rollback.
- Toggle ephemeral-warmpool marker persistence to survive backfill state transitions (Priya Nair) — prototype by 2026-02-15.
- Provider event correlation: contact provider ops to request raw eviction timeline for 2026-02-09 (Ava Morgan) — outreach sent 2026-02-11, expected response 48–72h.
- Customer comms: Customer Success prepare short blurb for impacted tenants (Marcus Holt) — draft by 2026-02-12.

5) Longer-term recommendations and hypotheses
- Revisit slot consolidation tradeoffs: consolidation improves cost-per-token but magnifies tenant surface area on preemption. Need a knob that is region-aware and sensitive to provider preemption probability (per-hourized signal).
- Backfill-safe routing: add a routing predicate that avoids nodes with backfill activity in the last X seconds for latency-sensitive tiers. Could be implemented as an opt-in at routing layer (console flag).
- Warm-pool durability: store warm markers in lightweight metadata attached to the node lifecycle rather than ephemeral memory, so they survive transient orchestration events. Evaluate SLOs for marker-consistency.

6) Runbook & operator steps (quick)
- If eu-west-1 partial-backfill ratio > 10% sustained for 6h: escalate to infra lead + open incident channel.
- Immediate mitigation: set slot-consolidation-threshold = 0.67 (rollback value) and increase warmpool-probe-interval to 15s for the affected region.
- If customer-visible errors persist after rollback: enable per-tenant auto-fallback to regional-standby models for affected tenants (requires console toggle).

7) Open questions / unresolved
- How often are provider-side preemption bursts correlated with other tenants in the same zone vs cross-zone? (we need provider timeline).
- Does our scheduler's backfill path evict KV slices more aggressively than necessary? If yes, can we prioritize KV retention for active sessions while evicting idle allocations first?
- Risk: making warm markers durable could increase metadata churn and slightly slow provisioning; need a perf budget.

8) Misc small notes and scribbles
- Observed a strange trace where two warm nodes got swapped mid-request (trace id: 2a7f-ops-evict-20260209) — likely orchestration race; follow-up with release-eng.
- Marcus: customer impacted list has 7 tenants, 2 on Dedicated, 5 on Hosted (mixed routes).
- Zoe: propose adding a small canary job that intentionally triggers micro backfills in test zone to validate policy changes before region rollout.

9) Follow-ups for next check-in (2026-02-18)
- Status of rollback metrics (Daniel) — present backfill counts, tail latencies, error pages.
- Prototype for durable warm markers (Priya) — demo and perf numbers.
- Provider timeline (Ava) — confirm or deny correlation.
- Canary micro backfill job report (Zoe) — run and capture.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- JIRA-OPS-2147: ticket for eu-west-1 backfill spike
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/812 (slot consolidation rollback patch)
- Confluence: priming-runbook-v2 (working copy)

Notes to self: keep this doc informal; if we make decisions escalate to infra-digest and mark runbook changes as immutable only after 2 successful rollouts.

-- End of notes --
